questions.q: The most effective drug class in peptic ulcer disease is:
questions.exp: Antiacid secretory agents are the most effective (Book p261)

questions.q: Match the PUD drug class to its action.
questions.exp: Anti-secretory → ↓HCl; gastroprotective → covers ulcer; antacids → neutralize HCl (Book p261)

questions.q: Match the anti-secretory drug group to its book fact.
questions.exp: PPIs = DOC; H2 blockers; anticholinergics pirenzepine/telenzepine inhibit M1 receptors (Book p261)

questions.q: Pirenzepine and telenzepine reduce acid by:
questions.exp: Anticholinergics pirenzepine, telenzepine inhibit M1 receptors (Book p261)

questions.q: Match the cell/structure to its acid-secretion role.
questions.exp: D-cells → somatostatin ⊣ gastrin; G-cells → gastrin; ECL → histamine → H2; ganglion M1 → ACh → M3 (Book p261)

questions.q: H. pylori kills ____ cells, removing somatostatin's brake and causing ↑ HCl secretion.
questions.exp: H. pylori kills D-cells → causes ↑HCl secretion (Book p261)

questions.q: On the parietal cell, the H+ pumps are stimulated (+) via which receptor set?
questions.exp: Histamine→H2, ACh→M3, gastrin→CCK-2B all (+) the H+ pumps → HCl secretion (Book p261)

questions.q: Somatostatin from D-cells ____ gastrin release.
questions.exp: Somatostatin blocks (X) gastrin (Book p261)

questions.q: Natezepide is best described as:
opts: A CCK-2B receptor blocker used for Rx of gastrinoma
A H2 blocker for post-op pneumonia prophylaxis
A gastrin analogue for diagnostic testing
questions.exp: Natezepide: CCK-2B receptor blocker; use: Rx of gastrinoma (Book p261)

questions.q: Natezepide blocks ____ receptors.
questions.exp: CCK-2B receptor blocker (Book p261)

questions.q: The half-life of PPIs is ____ hours.
questions.exp: Half life: 1.5–2 hours (Book p262)

questions.q: Despite a short half-life, PPIs are long acting because they are ____ inhibitors.
questions.exp: Long acting drugs (irreversible inhibitors) (Book p262)

questions.q: After stopping a PPI, the drug effect stops in ____ days.
questions.exp: On stopping drug → 3–5 days → drug effect stops (Book p262)

questions.q: PPIs are acid labile (broken down by HCl); the breakdown is maximum with ____.
questions.exp: Acid labile: maximum with rabeprazole (Book p262)

questions.q: Acid lability of PPIs is minimum with ____.
questions.exp: Acid labile: minimum with pantoprazole (Book p262)

questions.q: PPIs are taken ____ minutes before food.
questions.exp: Taken 30–60 mins before food (Book p262)

questions.q: Inside the parietal cell, oral PPI is converted to active PPI by:
opts: HCl (acid activation, boosted by food intake)
questions.exp: Oral PPI → HCl → active PPI in parietal cell; food intake (+) the process (Book p262)

questions.q: Match the PPI to its feature.
right: S-enantiomer alone → longer acting than omeprazole
Longest, fastest acting and most potent PPI
questions.exp: Omeprazole most potent enzyme inhibitor; esomeprazole S-enantiomer longer acting; pantoprazole least potent enzyme inhibitor; rabeprazole longest/fastest/most potent PPI (Book p262)

questions.q: Omeprazole is a racemic mixture of two enantiomers; the S-enantiomer is characterized by:
questions.exp: Racemic: S (slow elimination) & R (Book p262)

questions.q: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19. All of the following follow EXCEPT:
questions.exp: CYP2C19 inhibition blocks clopidogrel ACTIVATION → ↓ effect (not ↑); blocks metabolism of antidepressants/antipsychotics → ↑toxicity; blocks tamoxifen activation → ↓effect (Book p262)

questions.q: Omeprazole inhibits the activation of ____ , lowering its antiplatelet effect.
questions.exp: Inhibits activation of clopidogrel → ↓effect (Book p262)

questions.q: The PPI that is longer acting than omeprazole is ____.
questions.exp: Esomeprazole: S-enantiomer alone → longer acting than omeprazole (Book p262)

questions.q: The least potent enzyme inhibitor among PPIs is:
questions.exp: Pantoprazole: least potent enzyme inhibitor (Book p262)

questions.q: The longest, fastest acting and most potent PPI is:
questions.exp: Rabeprazole: longest, fastest acting PPI; most potent PPI (Book p262)

questions.q: Life-long PPI treatment is indicated for:
questions.exp: Barrett's esophagus — life long Rx (Book p263)

questions.q: In acute gastric bleed (I/V route), PPIs promote coagulation by providing a basic ____.
questions.exp: Provides basic pH → promotes coagulation (Book p263)

questions.q: PPI-induced ↓HCl causes ↑ microbial growth in stomach, raising the risk of pneumonia and ____.
questions.exp: ↑ microbial growth → ↑ risk of pneumonia, pseudomembranous enterocolitis (Book p263)

questions.q: PPI-induced ↓ absorption of which ion causes osteoporosis → hip fracture?
questions.exp: ↓ Ca++ absorption → PPI-induced osteoporosis → hip fracture (Book p263)

questions.q: Atrophic gastritis with PPIs lowers absorption of Ca++, ____, vitamin B12 and iron.
questions.exp: ↓ absorption of Ca++, Mg++, vitamin B12, iron (Book p263)

questions.q: The third listed PPI side effect, after ↓HCl effects and atrophic gastritis, is ____.
questions.exp: 3. Hypergastrinemia (Book p263)

questions.q: The least potent, shortest acting H2 blocker is ____.
questions.exp: Cimetidine: least potent, shortest acting (Book p263)

questions.q: The H2 blocker that is an enzyme inhibitor with (+) drug interactions is:
questions.exp: Cimetidine: enzyme inhibitor → drug interactions (+) (Book p263)

questions.q: The most potent, longest acting H2 blocker is ____.
questions.exp: Famotidine: most potent, longest acting (Book p263)

questions.q: H2 blockers are DOC in prevention of post-operative aspiration pneumonia because they block ____ acid secretion.
questions.exp: Basal acid secretion blocked (Book p263)

questions.q: Neurotoxicity (agitation, hallucination) with H2 blockers is favoured by which risk factors?
questions.exp: Risk factors: I/V route, elderly, cimetidine (Book p263)

questions.q: Cardiotoxicity (↓HR, ↓BP) with rapid I/V H2-blocker infusion is due to blockade of ____ receptors.
questions.exp: Rapid I/V infusion → blocks Gs-receptors → ↓HR, ↓BP (Book p263)

questions.q: To prevent H2-blocker cardiotoxicity, the infusion should be given over ____ minutes.
questions.exp: Prevention: infusion over 30 minutes (Book p263)

questions.q: Antiandrogenic effect (gynaecomastia, impotence) in males and ↑ prolactin → galactorrhoea in females are seen with:
questions.exp: Cimetidine: antiandrogenic in males; ↑prolactin → galactorrhoea in females (Book p264)

questions.q: Misoprostol is a prostaglandin ____ analogue.
questions.exp: Prostaglandin E1 analogue (Book p264)

questions.q: Match the gastroprotective agent to its mechanism.
right: Polymerised by gastric HCl → thick viscous cover over ulcer
Covers ulcer base, induces mucin/HCO3- synthesis, antibacterial
questions.exp: Misoprostol EP2/EP4 (Gs) ↑mucin & HCO3-, EP3 (Gi) ↓HCl; sucralfate polymerises by HCl; bismuth covers + mucin/HCO3- + antibacterial; antacids neutralize (Book p264)

questions.q: Misoprostol dose for NSAID-induced ulcers is 200 mcg ____ (frequency).
questions.exp: Dose: 200 mcg QID (Book p264)

questions.q: The most specific drug for NSAID-induced ulcers is ____.
questions.exp: Most specific drug: misoprostol (Book p264)

questions.q: Even though misoprostol is most specific, the DOC for NSAID-induced ulcers is ____.
questions.exp: DOC: PPI (Book p264)

questions.q: Misoprostol's side effects are:
questions.exp: S/E: severe abdominal cramps, diarrhoea (Book p264)

questions.q: Misoprostol is contraindicated in ____.
questions.exp: Contraindication: inflammatory bowel disease (Book p264)

questions.q: Sucralfate is ____ of sucrose + aluminium.
questions.exp: Octasulfate of sucrose + aluminium (Book p264)

questions.q: Oral sucralfate is polymerised by gastric ____ into a thick viscous substance covering the ulcer.
questions.exp: Polymerised by gastric HCl (Book p264)

questions.q: Besides PUD and esophageal ulcer, sucralfate is used for:
questions.exp: Uses: PUD, esophageal ulcer, prophylaxis of radiation proctitis (Book p264)

questions.q: Sucralfate's side effects include:
questions.exp: S/E: hypophosphatemia, gastric bezoars, constipation (Book p264)

questions.q: Sucralfate is contraindicated in ____ due to risk of aluminium toxicity (osteoporosis, encephalopathy).
questions.exp: Renal failure: risk of aluminium toxicity → osteoporosis, encephalopathy (Book p264)

questions.q: ____ prevent sucralfate polymerisation, so they must be kept apart in timing.
questions.exp: Antacids prevent polymerisation (Book p264)

questions.q: The two bismuth compounds are bismuth subsalicylate and bismuth ____.
questions.exp: Bismuth subsalicylate, bismuth subcitrate (Book p264)

questions.q: Bismuth compounds' mechanism includes all EXCEPT:
opts: Induces mucin and HCO3- synthesis at ulcer site
questions.exp: Bismuth covers ulcer base, induces mucin/HCO3-, antibacterial — it does not systemically neutralize HCl (Book p264)

questions.q: Bismuth causes blackish discolorisation of tongue and ____.
questions.exp: Blackish discolorisation of tongue & stool (Book p264)

questions.q: Bismuth subsalicylate is C/I in a child with fever because of ____ syndrome.
questions.exp: B. subsalicylate → Reye's syndrome (C/I in child with fever) (Book p264)

questions.q: The bismuth compound that causes neurotoxicity is bismuth ____.
questions.exp: B. subcitrate → neurotoxic (Book p264)

questions.q: Match the antacid salt to its bowel effect.
right: Effects cancelled out by each other
questions.exp: Magnesium → diarrhoea; aluminium → constipation; combination cancels out (Book p265)

questions.q: In PUD, the primary aim of antacids is ____ healing; the secondary aim is Rx of dyspepsia.
questions.exp: Primary aim: ulcer healing; secondary aim: Rx of dyspepsia (Book p265)

questions.q: Dosing of antacids in a complicated ulcer with bleeding (+) is:
questions.exp: Complicated ulcer [bleeding (+)] → every 30 mins (Book p265)

questions.q: For an uncomplicated ulcer, antacids are given ____ hours after food.
questions.exp: Uncomplicated ulcer → 1 & 3 hours after food (Book p265)

questions.q: In GERD, the DOC in pregnancy & children is ____.
questions.exp: GERD: DOC in pregnancy & children (antacids) (Book p265)

questions.q: Antacids are contraindicated with other drugs (interaction with Mg2+/Al3+) and in:
questions.exp: Contraindications: other drugs (D/t interaction with Mg2+/Al3+), renal failure (Book p265)

questions.q: Alginate absorbs water in stomach and floats above food to prevent ____; use: GERD.
questions.exp: Floats above food → prevents reflux; use: GERD (Book p265)

questions.q: Simethicone relieves flatulence by acting as a:
opts: Surfactant that ↓ surface tension of gas bubbles → rupture
questions.exp: Surfactant → ↓surface tension of gas bubbles → rupture → eases passage of gas, ↓foaming; use: flatulence, GERD (Book p265)

units.title: PUD Drug Classification
units.guide: Anti-secretory (most effective, ↓HCl): PPIs (DOC), H2 blockers, anticholinergics pirenzepine/telenzepine (M1). Gastroprotective: cover ulcer — sucralfate, bismuth, misoprostol. Antacids: neutralize HCl.

units.title: Physiology of Acid Secretion
units.guide: D-cells → somatostatin ⊣ gastrin; H. pylori kills D-cells → ↑HCl. G-cells → gastrin (+) ECL & (+) CCK-2B. ECL → histamine → H2. Ganglion M1 → ACh → M3. Parietal H+ pumps → HCl.

units.title: Natezepide Note
units.guide: Natezepide: CCK-2B receptor blocker; use: Rx of gastrinoma.

units.title: PPI Pharmacokinetics
units.guide: t½ 1.5–2 h but long acting (irreversible); effect stops 3–5 days after stopping; acid labile — max rabeprazole, min pantoprazole; taken 30–60 min before food; activated by HCl in parietal cell (food +).

units.title: PPI Features Table
units.guide: Omeprazole: most potent enzyme inhibitor, racemic (S slow elimination), CYP2C19 inhibition → ↑toxicity antidepressants/antipsychotics, ↓tamoxifen & ↓clopidogrel activation. Esomeprazole longer acting. Pantoprazole least potent enzyme inhibitor. Rabeprazole longest/fastest/most potent PPI.

units.title: PPI Uses and Side Effects
units.sec: PPI Uses and Side Effects · p263
units.guide: DOC: PUD, stress ulcers, NSAID ulcers, GERD, ZES; Barrett's life-long. Acute gastric bleed IV → basic pH → coagulation. S/E: ↓HCl → pneumonia/pseudomembranous enterocolitis; atrophic gastritis → ↓Ca++/Mg++/B12/iron; hypergastrinemia.

units.title: H2-Receptor Blockers
units.guide: Cimetidine least potent/shortest + enzyme inhibitor + antiandrogenic/↑prolactin. Famotidine most potent/longest. DOC post-op aspiration pneumonia (basal acid blocked). Neurotoxicity risk: IV, elderly, cimetidine. Rapid IV → blocks Gs → ↓HR/↓BP; infuse over 30 min.

units.title: Misoprostol
units.guide: PGE1 analogue; EP2/EP4 (Gs) ↑mucin & HCO3-, EP3 (Gi) ↓HCl. NSAID ulcers: 200 mcg QID; most specific misoprostol but DOC PPI. S/E cramps/diarrhoea; C/I inflammatory bowel disease.

units.title: Sucralfate
units.guide: Octasulfate of sucrose + aluminium; polymerised by gastric HCl → viscous cover. Uses PUD, esophageal ulcer, radiation proctitis prophylaxis. S/E hypophosphatemia, bezoars, constipation. C/I renal failure; antacids prevent polymerisation.

units.title: Bismuth Compounds
units.guide: Subsalicylate & subcitrate. Cover ulcer base, induce mucin/HCO3-, antibacterial. Uses PUD, traveller's diarrhoea, H. pylori. Black tongue/stool; subsalicylate → Reye's (C/I child with fever); subcitrate → neurotoxic.

units.title: Antacids
units.guide: Mg → diarrhoea, Al → constipation, combination cancels. PUD: primary ulcer healing, secondary dyspepsia. Bleeding ulcer: every 30 min; uncomplicated: 1 & 3 h after food. GERD DOC in pregnancy & children. C/I renal failure, with other drugs.

units.title: Add-on Antacids
units.guide: Alginate: floats above food → prevents reflux (GERD). Simethicone: surfactant → ruptures gas bubbles → flatulence, GERD.
